name: Chike-Taman Pass
full: Chike-Taman Pass on the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway), a spur of the Terekta Range, between the villages of Khabarovka (northern slope, Ursul valley) and Kupchegen (southern slope, Bolshoy Ilgumen valley)
near: Khabarovka village (≈9 km, fuel station), Kupchegen village (southern descent), Ongudai village (≈25–27 km, district center)
elev: 1295 m (Great Russian Encyclopedia; amic.ru; most sources); SibGid gives 1460 m — a discrepancy
short: The second-highest pass on the Chuysky Trakt (1295 m, ≈km 659) with a steep serpentine road in granite cliffs, a viewing platform, a monument to road builders and a view of the abandoned old road.
desc: Chike-Taman (“flat sole” in Altai) is a pass over a spur of the Terekta Range on the Chuysky Trakt, the watershed of the Ursul and the Bolshoy Ilgumen (according to other sources, the Maly and Bolshoy Ilgumen). The height is 1295 m, the pass is at km 659 of the highway (km 663 in the amic.ru article), and the climb and descent are about 4 km on each side (11 km of climb and descent combined per the Great Russian Encyclopedia). Traces of an ancient road here date from the 10th–12th centuries; by 1903 a pack trail with 34 sharp bends had been built, and cars first crossed the pass in 1924–1925. The modern paved road opened in 1984: more than 500,000 tonnes of earth were moved and about a dozen rocks blown up; the old narrow gravel road is still visible on the slope. Since 1996 the pass has been a natural monument of the Altai Republic (112.5 ha), valued also as a “monument of road construction of different eras”. The slopes are made of Cambrian-Ordovician sandstones and shales, and the pass has larch forests, rhododendron and edelweiss; in early spring yellow tulips bloom on the southern slopes. At the top there is a viewing platform with parking, vendor stalls (shashlik, chebureki, herbal tea, souvenirs), a cast-iron monument to road builders (2017), and a sacred larch with dyalama ribbons.
guide: Don't just drive over the pass — park at the viewing platform and walk to the edge: below you can see the winding old road along which all the trucks to Mongolia drove until 1984. Drivers used to call the pass “Chert-Ataman” (“Devil Chieftain”) — look at the serpentine and you'll understand why. The ribbons on the larch are dyalama, an offering to the spirits of the pass: if you tie your own, take only a white or light one and don't touch other people's. Get herbal tea and a cheburek from the locals — it is a classic of the stop. The best light is in the morning on the northern side and at sunset on the southern valley.
see: The viewing platform at the summit (the tour description mentions three viewpoints on the pass); a view of the old road of 1903–1984; the monument to the road worker (2017); the sacred larch with ribbons; a panorama of mountains of 2500–2600 m; the granite rock cuts of the serpentine; in spring — yellow tulips and rhododendron.
skip: You are driving the highway in winter in icy conditions or in fog: a stop at the viewpoint will show nothing anyway, and the serpentine demands attention. If you are heading to Kalbak-Tash and the Chuya with children who get carsick on serpentines — get out to stretch your legs only at the top.
diff: Easy: a paved approach, a few dozen meters from the parking area to the viewpoint
when: Late spring to mid-autumn; autumn (September to early October) is the most colorful time (Bolshaya Strana). In winter the pass is passable, but ice is possible.
hours: Around the clock, free (an open area by the federal highway); vendor stalls mostly in the warm season (hours not found)
daytime: Morning and evening — soft side light on the serpentine (editorial); on summer days the parking area is crowded
how: Along the Chuysky Trakt R-256: from Gorno-Altaysk ≈220–230 km (Ongudai is 200 km from Gorno-Altaysk, then ≈25 km more), from Biysk ≈310–320 km, from Barnaul 8–9 h by car. By public transport — the Gorno-Altaysk–Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus) (09:00) goes over the pass, a stop at the summit by arrangement with the driver; catching a passing service back is hard. The most convenient way is your own car or an excursion.
needcar: Yes — a car, an excursion or a scheduled marshrutka (minibus) along the highway
self: Yes, fully: paved road, parking at the summit, no permits needed
roadtype: Paved road of the federal highway R-256, a serpentine of ≈4 km of climb and ≈4 km of descent; the old road is dirt/gravel and abandoned
traveltime: From Gorno-Altaysk ≈3–3.5 h by car (marshrutka (minibus) to Ongudai 2 h 50 min + ≈25 km); from Biysk ≈5 h; from Ongudai ≈30 min
stay: None on the pass. Nearby: the Chike Taman recreation base (Kupchegen village, R-256 highway, 16; from 2000 ₽, opens in May — 2GIS 2026), the Ilgumen tourist base (km 669); Ongudai — Khutorok (from 1500 ₽), Kok-Boru (from 800 ₽); Maly Yaloman — Baylyk, Ail (from 2500 ₽)
net: not found (no data on operator coverage at the summit)
entry: Free (a natural monument by the highway). According to a 2GIS review, the climb to the upper viewpoint is paid, 100 ₽ (there is a terminal; year not given); the toilet is paid. There is no resort fee in the Altai Republic.
transfer: Excursions from Gorno-Altaysk 8000–12,900 ₽/person (2026); individual 27,965 ₽ per group of up to 6
bring: A warm jacket/windbreaker (the weather changes sharply), cash for vendors, water and a snack, sun protection
warn: A serpentine with sharp bends — don't stop on the roadside outside the platform. Ice and snow are possible from autumn to spring. A seismically active area (tremors of the 2003 Chuya earthquake were felt). Don't go along the old road to the edge of the rock cuts. R-256 repairs in 2026: in the Altai Republic km 439–444 (Maima) and 560–570 (exit from Shebalino) have been repaired; work continues until the end of 2026 at km 455–472 (Souzga–Manzherok) and 479–495 (Izvestkovy–Barangol) — narrowing and reversing traffic are possible (Tolk, 06.10.2026). In 2026–2029 an 18 km reconstruction near Souzga–Manzherok with detours (Tolk, 24.03.2026). On 01.10.2026 a rockfall onto the highway without casualties was reported (NGS22; location not specified). The highway is periodically closed for military convoys. There is no border zone here. Ticks: according to Rospotrebnadzor for the Altai Republic, by 25.08.2026 there were 3600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Ongudai district is among the districts with bites). Payment terminals in villages work unreliably — bring cash (OneTwoTrip, 10.2024). Parking at the summit is small, and on the approach there is a “no stopping” sign and yellow markings: don't stop on the serpentine (2GIS reviews).
food: The “Hello Chike-Taman” canteen in Khabarovka village (Severnaya St., 23; 4.8 from 122 ratings, bill ≈450 ₽, 2GIS 2026); chebureki, shashlik and herbal tea at the vendor stalls on the pass; in Ongudai — Leto na Altae (“Summer in Altai”) (bill ≈350 ₽), Nikitka (manty and pelmeni made from maral venison), Altyn (Altai cuisine)
reviews: 2GIS: 5.0 (1828–1834 ratings, 242 reviews, 2026); Google: 4.9 (3532 reviews, per Wanderlog). Separately on 2GIS: “Chike Taman old road” — 4.0 (2), Chike-Taman souvenir markets — 3.5–5.0. Pros: views, the serpentine, the old road, a convenient platform. Cons: crowded in summer, trading and paid photos in costumes.
